**Atlas Docs** — Launch a technical docs portal that gets new users to hello world in under 5 minutes.

**Stack:** next • typescript • tailwind • tests: vitest

**Project type:** `docs-portal`

> Source of truth: `.project-spine/spine.json` (hash `cbac2972d9a29995`). Every rule below has a traceable source. If a rule is wrong, fix the upstream input (`brief.md`, repo state, or `design-rules.md`) and rerun `spine compile`.

## Repo conventions

- Use the Next.js App Router (`app/`). Prefer server components by default; only opt into client components via `"use client"` when needed.
- Style exclusively with Tailwind utility classes. Do not add inline `style` props or ad-hoc CSS unless the component is outside the design system.
- TypeScript strict mode is on. Never use `any`; prefer `unknown` + narrow at the boundary.

## Do / Don't

- Prefer small, focused diffs. One concern per PR or patch.
- Always show the exact test or typecheck command you ran and its result.
- When following a rule from this file, cite it by section heading so reviewers can audit.
- Do not refactor code unrelated to the task, even if it looks better.
- Do not add new dependencies without flagging the choice and reason.
- When adding a guide, cross-link it from the nearest landing / index page and the top-level guides index.
- Do not write guides as prose walls. Use headings, code blocks, and short paragraphs.

## Never do this (unsafe)

- Never modify generated files (anything under `dist/`, `build/`, `.next/`, or marked `@generated`).
- Never edit lockfiles manually.
- Never commit secrets. Redact any `.env*` content that appears in logs or diffs.

## File placement

- Pages go in `app/`. Route segments use `page.tsx`. Shared UI goes in `components/` or `src/components/`.

## Response expectations

- Before claiming work is complete, run the repo's typecheck and test commands and show the output.
- If the brief is ambiguous on a specific section, ask rather than guess. Cite the section heading.

## Component & design rules

- Sidebar — Nested nav with active-state highlighting and collapsible sections.
- TOC — Right-rail table of contents with scroll-spy.
- CodeBlock — Copy button, language label, line highlights.
- Callout — Info / warning / success variants with proper semantics.
- SearchBar — Instant search with keyboard-only navigation of results.
- VersionSwitcher — Version-aware navigation where applicable.

## Accessibility baseline

- All interactive elements must be reachable and operable with the keyboard alone.
- Focus must be visible at all times; never remove outlines without replacing them.
- Text contrast must meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text).
- Every form control has a programmatic label.
- Pages use proper landmark regions (header, main, nav, footer) and a sensible heading order.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for any non-essential animation.
- Skip-to-content link is the first focusable element.
- Code block copy buttons have an aria-label and visible focus state.

## UX rules

- Guides are task-oriented, not concept-oriented; each one ends with 'Next steps' that link forward.
- Landing hero contains a runnable quickstart, not marketing.

## QA guardrails

- Unit tests live next to source as `*.test.ts`. Run `vitest run` in CI and before every commit touching business logic.
- `tsc --noEmit` must pass on every PR.
- Success criterion to verify before launch: Quickstart command sequence runs from a clean machine without edits.
- Success criterion to verify before launch: Broken-link count is zero in CI.
- Success criterion to verify before launch: Every generated reference page links back to its source.
- Docs build passes on every PR; broken-link check enforced.
- Search index rebuild runs on each deploy.
- Every code block is copy-verified (pastes + runs without edit).
- All generated reference pages link back to source.

## What we are building (from brief)

- Launch a technical docs portal that gets new users to hello world in under 5 minutes.
- Keep guides, reference pages, and changelog entries versioned with the repo.
- Make stale docs fail CI through broken-link and copyable-code checks.

## Constraints

- Docs are Markdown/MDX in the repo; no CMS for v1.
- API reference is generated from source metadata during build.
- Search index must rebuild on every deploy.

## Known risks

- Reference generation may lag behind source changes.
- Search quality can hide good docs if headings are inconsistent.
